answer: In an agent market trading shale shipments through a jetty, each seller identity must lock a $1,000 bond for 30 days before it can quote. Creating aliases therefore requires fresh collateral: 100 fake sellers tie up $100,000, with no reuse across identities during the lock. This makes a sybil spiral costly in proportion to its size, because the attacker pays financing costs and loses access to that capital even if every account behaves honestly.
